notes: Box score from the Orlando Magic's 113–111 road win over the Brooklyn Nets on Nov 20, 2026, from the Covers.com box score, checked against the Plain Text Sports game page and play-by-play, with game details from the Associated Press (via LA NACION), Field Level Media (via GMA News), the Orlando Sentinel and SB Nation (both via Yahoo Sports), WFTV and Heavy. All 113 Orlando points and all 111 Brooklyn points are accounted for in the box score, and the quarter scores (38–24–29–22 to 25–36–27–23) add up to both totals: 62–61 Orlando at the half and 91–88 after three. Team totals (threes 19 of 43 to 12 of 38, free throws 16 of 23 to 23 of 27, assists 24–24, blocks 6–3) are from the box score; points in the paint (36–48) and the biggest leads (Orlando 15, Brooklyn 7) are from the Covers.com box score, and Plain Text Sports gives the same leads. Records are from the game stories (the site's standings were not yet updated when this was built).

Orlando made 10 of 13 threes in the first quarter, a franchise record for a quarter (Orlando Sentinel; WFTV; Field Level Media), and led 40–25 early in the second (Plain Text Sports). Brooklyn opened the second on a 16–4 run and led 57–56 late in the half (Plain Text Sports). The fourth quarter had nine lead changes (WFTV). Jalen Suggs' 3-pointer at 3:22 made it 106–104, Mikel Brown Jr.'s and-one at 3:09 put Brooklyn up 107–106, Julius Randle's turnaround at 2:20 made it 109–106, Desmond Bane's step-back 3 at 2:00 tied it, and Randle's two free throws at 1:24 made it 111–109 (Plain Text Sports play-by-play; AP). Wendell Carter Jr.'s putback with 30.5 seconds left tied it at 111 (Plain Text Sports; AP; Field Level Media). Franz Wagner then hit the winner, and Randle's 28-foot step-back 3 at the buzzer missed (Plain Text Sports; Field Level Media; AP). Wagner scored 35 (AP). It was the first NBA game between Franz and his brother Moritz Wagner, who signed with Brooklyn in July (AP; Heavy). Orlando has won 10 straight over Brooklyn (Field Level Media), is 3–0 in the NBA Cup (WFTV; Orlando Sentinel) and has won 5 of its last 6 (AP); Brooklyn has lost four straight (AP). Orlando plays at Washington on Sunday and Brooklyn at Minnesota on Monday (Plain Text Sports schedule; AP).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Franz Wagner's step-back jumper with 2.8 seconds left that broke a 111–111 tie (Plain Text Sports play-by-play gives the clock, the score and a 15-foot step-back, unassisted; Field Level Media gives the clock, the inbound from Jalen Suggs out of an Orlando timeout and a 15-foot step-back over Noah Clowney and Randle; the AP, the Orlando Sentinel and SB Nation say 2.4 seconds left, the clock at Brooklyn's timeout after the make). The template draws a plain pull-up jumper, not the step-back itself. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Orlando Magic or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Franz Wagner's listed 6-foot-10 and 220 pounds with No. 22 (RealGM), with arms scaled to a reported 7-foot wingspan (CraftedNBA), in Orlando's road blue. He has no approved look on file yet, so he is drawn in the kit with the default figure. It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
